theater: 大馬士革至撒馬利亞戰線

battle.name: 以色列-亞蘭戰爭
battle.theater: 大馬士革至撒馬利亞戰線
battle.brief: 前733年，以色列王國撒馬利亞與亞蘭王朝大馬士革在北部黎凡特開戰。亞捫·哈達二世集結三十二國王的車馬聯軍圍攻撒馬利亞，亞哈王以三百首領守城、二百精兵伏於城中，會戰於阿貝克取勝，兵鋒直抵大馬士革城下。卡面的埃及長矛正是這場戰役中步兵的標準配備：青銅矛頭安於木杆，用於守城垣，也用於野戰中的近身衝鋒。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是北部黎凡特兩強的直接對撞。一方是以色列王國，首都撒馬利亞（示劍城南的丘陵城，即今巴勒斯坦塞巴斯蒂亞一帶），君主為暗利王朝的亞哈王；另一方是亞蘭王朝的大馬士革，君主為亞捫·哈達二世。以色列方面，亞哈承暗利留下的軍事底子：城內駐有車兵與騎兵，甲冑匠與馬廄集中在撒馬利亞，王室直接掌握數百名「首領」與一支精銳步兵；它的對外通道則由王后耶洗別那一邊經手——她是西頓推羅王的 女兒，這條商路帶來象牙、雪松與造車匠，也帶來巴力祭祀與西頓式車隊。以色列的城防核心是撒馬利亞本身：石砌城牆、坡面壘土與三重城門構成第一道防線，另有石砌水渠自示劍方向引水入城，攻城方最想切斷的正是這條水線。亞蘭方面是一個聯盟式軍隊國家：亞捫·哈達二世自稱召集「三十二個王」，各小邦按軍役、車乘與馬匹配額出兵，車列與營帳在南下途中不斷膨脹；亞軍的野戰統帥是乃縵，掌管大軍、先鋒與軍資，而糧秣靠大馬士革後方經貝卡谷地與阿爾卡河谷輸送，戰線每往南推一格，供養線就長一格。第三方包括猶大（耶洗華王與亞哈有姻親與同盟，兵員分開調度）、非利士人的迦特城，以及已退守尼羅河三角洲的埃及第二十二王朝——它早已失去為黎凡特提供緩衝的能力，卻仍以造車術與青銅武器祖源地的身份留在這場戰爭的裝備記憶裡。
countriesEn: This war was a direct collision between two powers of the northern Levant. On one side stood the Kingdom of Israel, its capital at Samaria, the hill city south of Shechem that today lies near Sebastia in the West Bank, ruled by King Ahab of the Omrid dynasty; on the other stood Damascus in the Aramean kingdom, ruled by Ben-Hadad II. The Israelite army inherited the base built by Omri: war chariots and horses were stationed in the capital, armourers and stables worked for the court, and the royal household directly commanded several hundred commanders plus a body of picked infantry. Israel's outward links ran through Jezebel, daughter of the king of Sidon-Tyre; that trading route brought ivory, cedar and chariot craftsmen, and with them the cult of Baal and a Tyrian style of carriage. The core of Israel's defence was Samaria itself: stone ramparts, glacis-style earthworks and a triple gate line made the first tier, while a stone aqueduct carried water into the city from the Shechem side, the one artery a besieger most wanted to cut. Aramean power was a coalition military state. Ben-Hadad II claimed the service of 'thirty kings', each small state supplying troops, chariots and horses by quota, with the columns and the camp growing as they marched south. Field command was held by Naaman, who directed the host, the vanguard and its supply, while the food and fodder of the army came north to south out of Damascus by way of the Beqaa and the Wadi al-'Arqa, so every stage of the advance lengthened the line of supply. Third parties were Judah, tied to Ahab by marriage and alliance through Jehoshaphat and keeping its own troops apart; the Philistine city of Gath; and the Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt, which had long since lost the ability to act as a buffer for the Levant but remained present in the equipment memory of this war as the ancestral home of the chariot and of the bronze spear.
people: 亞捫·哈達二世是主動挑戰的一方，此時已牢牢控制大馬士革與黎凡特北部的商路，慣以聯盟徵召小邦出兵。他統率的「三十二王」是策略性聯盟的原型：每個王各帶車隊與步兵，營帳分列，聯軍總規模在南下的路上不斷膨脹；乃縵這位亞軍元帥在《列王紀上》被描述為亞捫·哈達的左右手，掌管大軍與軍資。另一方的亞哈王是暗利王朝第二代君主，靠與推羅結姻、靠內政經營累積的富裕著稱，他做了一件前任不會做的事：拒絕繳納亞蘭索求的贖金，改以備戰應敵。他任命三百名首領分區訓練民眾，又把二百名精兵藏在城內，準備在會戰關鍵時刻投入奇襲。兒子約蘭王在父王死後即位，此時國庫已被他抵押給推羅王以換取援軍；正是他在圍城最危急時驅車出城去見以利沙，先知以一句話回覆了他。撒馬利亞的以利沙是先知圈的實際權力中心：他預言饑荒將在隔日結束，又用一套計策令亞軍自行退兵；他的門徒在亞軍首腦處取得情報，證明他對敵營的掌握深入到決策層。乃縵是亞軍統帥中與以利沙交情最深的一位，皈依耶和華並得醫治，讓亞以之間多出一條不經外交的個人管道。最後是哈及——亞捫·哈達身旁的侍臣兼軍官，他弒主自立為亞蘭王，隨後多年反覆進攻以色列、攻取迦特，把這場戰爭的平衡徹底傾斜；亞述文獻中的「圖瑪爾之王」一般即被認為是他，說明北方強權已在記錄他的名字。
peopleEn: Ben-Hadad II of Damascus was the aggressor. By then he held the trade routes of the northern Levant firmly and habitually summoned his vassal states into a coalition. The 'thirty kings' he led were the archetype of the coalition army: each king brought his own chariots and infantry, the tents stood in separate divisions, and the total size of the host kept growing as it marched south. Naaman, the commander of the army of Aram, is described in Kings as Ben-Hadad's right hand, holding the field army and its logistics. On the other side, Ahab, the second king of the Omrid line, was known for the wealth his house had piled up through a marriage with Tyre and through careful internal administration, and he did the one thing his predecessor would not have done: he refused to pay the Aramean ransom and prepared for war instead. He named three hundred commanders to drill the population district by district, and hid two hundred picked men inside the city for the moment when the battle would be decided. His son Jehoram succeeded him in the middle of the crisis, with the treasury already pledged to the king of Tyre in exchange for help, and it was Jehoram who drove out of the besieged city to consult Elisha and received a single sentence in reply. Elisha was the real centre of power in the prophetic circle at Samaria: he announced that the famine would end within the day, and he engineered the sudden collapse of the Aramean siege. His servant's access to the Aramean war council showed that his grasp of the enemy reached into the decision-making itself. Naaman was the Aramean commander closest to Elisha; his conversion and healing opened a personal channel between the two camps that bypassed formal diplomacy. Last came Hazael, an officer of Ben-Hadad's court who killed his master and took the throne, then campaigned against Israel year after year and took Gath, tilting the balance of the war permanently. The 'king of Tummar' named in the Assyrian records is generally identified with Hazael, which shows that the northern powers were already keeping his name on file.
kits: 卡面這支埃及長矛是理解這場戰爭兵器譜系的鑰匙：早王朝時期的埃及以銅或青銅矛頭、繩索纏束的方式安在木杆上，用於守城垣、護衛儀仗，也用於在尼羅河谷與西奈征戰中列陣推進。這種矛——有尾套、刃面狹長、為反覆刺擊而設計的樣式——經過青銅時代的西奈與迦南中介傳入黎凡特，在伯示安、美吉多一類城邑的守軍中成為標準配備。以色列與亞蘭交戰的年代雖然已入鐵器時代，長矛仍是步兵最可靠的近戰兵器：鐵矛頭安在白蠟木杆上，交戰時以盾護身、列陣前推，格殺的關鍵不在砍劈，而在能不能頂住對方的推進。聖經文獻裡「王的槍」「勇士的槍」正是近衛與王的武裝，說明長矛同時是身份標誌。真正決定這場戰爭節奏的仍是車馬：以色列與亞蘭都保有埃及式雙輪輕車，車上通常是一兵一御，車兵是全軍最銳利也最脆弱的部分，一台車需要兩匹馬、一套甲冑與大量侍從維持。弓仍是遠程主力，亞軍與以軍都有成建制的射手；盾牌以圓形小盾為主，配合長矛使用；鎧甲以鱗甲為主流，銅片與鐵片分給車兵與重裝步兵。攻城戰術上，圍城靠封鎖而非強攻：亞軍切斷示劍方向的水渠與谷地道路，令城內饑荒；亞哈則靠自己的車隊與輜重維持遠征大馬士革的行軍。值得注意的是《列王紀下》記載以利沙門徒「取鐵器」下到約旦河，說明當時的鐵已不只是兵器材料，也進入日常工具與工程用品，冶金業正是這條戰線背後的另一種軍備競賽。運輸方面，馬匹之外還靠騾子與驢子負載，貴重的銀錫與鎧甲都要靠馱獸運出山口。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is the key to the weapon system of this war. In the Early Dynastic period the Egyptians fixed copper or bronze blades to wooden shafts with cord binding, using them to defend walls, to carry in royal honour guards and to push ordered formations in the Nile valley and the Sinai campaigns. That pattern — socketed, narrow-bladed, designed for repeated thrusting rather than for the cut — reached the Levant through Canaanite intermediaries in the Bronze Age and became standard kit for the garrison troops of cities such as Beth-Shean and Megiddo. By the time Israel and Aram fought, the age of iron had begun, but the spear remained the infantryman's most reliable close-combat arm: an iron socketed blade on an ash shaft, carried behind a shield in a massed advance, where the point of the fight was not the cut but whether a line could hold the push. In the biblical text the 'spear of the king' and the 'spear of the mighty' are the weapons of the guard and of the ruler, which shows that the spear was also a badge of rank. Chariots and horses still set the tempo. Both sides kept the Egyptian two-wheeled light chariot, crewed by a driver and a warrior, the most offensive and most fragile part of any army, and a single vehicle demanded two horses, a set of armour and a substantial train of retainers. The bow remained the main missile arm, with formed bodies of archers on both sides; shields were mostly small round bucklers, used together with the spear; armour was scale armour, with bronze and iron plates going to chariot warriors and to heavy infantry. Siege work at this scale was a matter of blockade rather than of assault: the Arameans cut the aqueduct and the roads through the valley, and famine did the work a battering ram would have done, while Ahab kept his chariots and baggage train moving all the way to Damascus. One detail in Kings is telling: Elisha's men 'took the iron tools' down to the Jordan, which shows that by then iron had left the category of weapons altogether and entered tools and engineering equipment, so metallurgy was a second arms race running behind this front. Beyond horses, transport depended on mules and donkeys; silver, tin and armour all had to leave the passes on pack animals.
tactics: 亞捫·哈達的戰術起點是車馬的集結與壓制：三十二王的聯軍在阿貝克一帶扎營，車列在前、步兵列陣於後，待令於平原；隨即南下圍困撒馬利亞，採取封鎖而非強攻——切斷示劍方向的水渠、封住通往耶斯列的谷道、封鎖城郊道路，用饑荒代替攻城錘。以色列的守城戰術是「深壁固守、間隙出擊」：城牆與壘土構成第一道防線，亞哈把三百名首領分派到各區組織守備，又挑出二百名精兵藏在城內，準備在會戰關鍵時刻加入。以利沙一方則把主動權轉到諜報與心理層面：亞軍在城下的會議內容被門徒聽到，計策是斷水；以色列人反其道而行，在約旦河上游的森林裡設伏，用成隊的「甲士」驚動林中的禽鳥、造出戰車與馬匹的巨響，亞軍判斷援兵已到，當夜棄營而走，圍城就這樣不解自解。阿貝克會戰則是標準的守方反擊：以色列列營與亞軍隔營對峙七天，等亞軍出營列陣才投入全軍，隱蔽的二百精兵從另一側出現，亞軍崩潰，國王換馬逃回大馬士革。追擊戰把戰場推到亞蘭本土，亞哈一度兵臨大馬士革城下，但未能攻下，遂轉為談判。整體看，這場戰爭的勝負手不在正面廝殺，而在水與糧的時間競賽：守方能撐多久，取決於城內存糧與水渠是否被切斷；攻方能撐多久，取決於從大馬士革經貝卡谷地與阿爾卡河谷的補給線有多長，兩條線都靠地形決定節奏。馬車在會戰中的角色是衝鋒與追擊，一旦距離拉開，車兵反而成為攻方最脆弱的一環。
tacticsEn: Ben-Hadad's plan began with the massing of chariots and horses. The allied camp stood near Aphek with the chariot line in front and the infantry drawn up behind, waiting for orders on the plain, and from there it moved south to invest Samaria, choosing blockade over assault — cutting the aqueduct on the Shechem side, sealing the valley road to Jezreel, closing the tracks around the city, so that famine replaced the ram. Israel's defence combined deep walls with a counter-stroke. The ramparts and earthworks were the first line, Ahab distributed three hundred commanders to organise the watch district by district, and two hundred picked men were hidden inside the city to be committed at the decisive moment. Elisha's side shifted the initiative to intelligence and morale. The Aramean council below the city was overheard, and the plan to cut the water was answered from the other side: bands were posted in the woods above the Jordan who startled the birds and manufactured the noise of chariots and horses, the enemy read it as relief armies arriving, broke camp that night, and the siege dissolved without a blow. The battle at Aphek was a textbook counter-attack by the defenders. The Israelite camp faced the Aramean camp across the plain for seven days, waited for the enemy to come out in line, then committed the whole army while the hidden two hundred appeared on the other flank; the Aramean line collapsed and the king escaped on horseback to Damascus. The pursuit carried the war into Aram, where Ahab brought his army under the walls of Damascus, failed to take the city and turned to negotiation. Taken as a whole, this war was decided less by pitched battle than by a race against water and grain. How long the besieged could hold depended on the stores inside the walls and on whether the aqueduct was cut; how long the besiegers could hold depended on the length of the supply line running from Damascus through the Beqaa and the Wadi al-'Arqa. Chariots were the shock arm of the decision in the open field, and once the lines separated they became the most vulnerable part of the attack.
data: 這場戰爭的數字主要來自《列王紀》的敘述，多屬文學性與神學性的數目，不能當作經審計的傷亡與兵力統計，但仍可看出戰役的規模輪廓。第一次圍城前，亞捫·哈達集結「三十二個王」與車馬；撒馬利亞城內，亞哈安排三百名首領分區訓練，二百名精兵隱蔽待命；阿貝克會戰打了七天，《列王紀上》記亞軍陣亡二萬七千人，並記亞哈擊敗後圍困大馬士革。和約的書面條件裡出現了車千乘與步兵萬計的數目，說明以、亞之間的實力比較是以車隊為尺度，而不是以步兵人數為尺度。圍城期的饑荒被描述為漫長到「我們等候我們的孩子」的地步，亞軍在城下至少跨過一個收穫季。第二段記載裡，亞捫·哈達的元帥乃縵為求醫治而帶來兩匹騾子馱銀，並在約旦河浸了七次；約蘭王則以一他連得銀與一他連得金的價碼去換推羅王的援兵。以利沙在迦密山對抗的巴力先知與亞舍拉先知名單，也是當時宗教—政治體系的量度。地理上，大馬士革至撒馬利亞的陸路約一百三十至一百五十公里，中間隔著貝卡谷地與阿爾卡河谷；亞軍每次南下都要把這段距離連同水源一起帶在身後。年份需要說明：條目沿用戰爭列表所標的前733年，但《列王紀》所記諸役在學界通常置於亞哈與約蘭王統治的九世紀中葉，兩者有出入，本條目依列表登錄；史書未載起事月份，表中月份取自行軍與圍城的農業節奏，屬推定值而非原文。
dataEn: The figures for this war come mainly from the narrative of Kings. They are literary and theological numbers rather than audited returns of casualties and strengths, but they still show the outline of the scale involved. Before the first siege Ben-Hadad mustered 'thirty kings' with their chariots and horses; inside Samaria, Ahab posted three hundred commanders to drill the population by district and kept two hundred picked men concealed in reserve; the battle at Aphek lasted seven days, and the text records twenty-seven thousand Arameans falling, followed by Ahab's siege of Damascus. The written terms of the settlement are expressed in thousands of chariots and tens of thousands of foot, which shows that the comparison between Israel and Aram was made in chariots rather than in infantry numbers. The famine during the siege is described as lasting long enough for mothers to say they were waiting for their children, so the Aramean camp stood outside the city across at least one harvest. In the second cycle, Naaman brought two mules laden with silver in order to obtain healing and dipped seven times in the Jordan, while Jehoram offered a talent of silver and a talent of gold in exchange for the Tyrian king's assistance. The list of Baal prophets and Asherah prophets confronted by Elisha on Mount Carmel measures the religious and political structure of the age. Geographically, the land route from Damascus to Samaria runs about 130 to 150 kilometres with the Beqaa and the Wadi al-'Arqa in between, and every Aramean column marching south had to carry that distance and its water along with it. A note on the dating: this entry follows the war list, which places the conflict in 733 BC, but the episodes of Kings are usually placed by scholars in the mid-ninth century BC, in the reigns of Ahab and Jehoram, so the two differ, and the catalogue keeps the year given by the list. The sources give no month for the opening of the war; the month entered in the table is an inference from the agricultural rhythm of campaigning and siege, not a reading from the text.
cause: 戰爭的深層原因有三層。第一層是黎凡特的權力真空：西元前十二世紀海上民族之後，埃及退守尼羅河三角洲，第二十二王朝的諸王在塔尼斯、布巴斯蒂斯等城分據，無力再為黎凡特提供緩衝，亞蘭從一個邊陲小邦變成北部黎凡特的強權，而北以色列正卡在它與埃及之間。第二層是暗利王朝的治理難題：亞哈的祖父暗利以賄賂、聯姻與分地換取安寧，把迦密山、示劍等地從邊境諸邦收編為王國核心，又以耶洗別的西頓婚盟引入推羅的商船、象牙與造車匠，使撒馬利亞富甲一方；這種繁榮同時招來兩種指責——先知批評王室巴力祭祀，亞述與亞蘭的使節則衡量它的可攻略程度。第三層是觸發事件：亞捫·哈達先以聯軍逼繳貢金，又要求以色列歸還被奪的城邑，亞哈一度準備以財貨贖買，卻在城門下被當眾羞辱，話語把「一捧塵土」與撒馬利亞的財富相提並論，談判的餘地因此歸零。正當亞捫·哈達步步進逼之際，亞哈王朝內部因拿伯的葡萄園（耶斯列）爆發血案，亞哈用計殺死拿伯、奪其田產，恰好在亞軍壓境之時把耶斯列平原這塊肥沃的引水田推上戰桌——水源、耕地與道路正是亞蘭南下的真正目標。宗教層面是先知與王室的正面衝突：以利亞在迦密山宣布旱災、要求交出巴力先知，等於宣告亞捫·哈達的盟邦網與亞希雅的神權在乾旱面前同時失效。當然，兩位國王的自尊也推了一把：亞捫·哈達羞辱贖金的做法，直接把可以談判的危機變成必須靠戰鬥解決的危機。
causeEn: There are three layers of cause behind the war. The first is the power vacuum in the Levant. After the Sea Peoples of the twelfth century BC, Egypt withdrew behind the Nile delta, and the kings of the Twenty-second Dynasty, split between Tanis, Bubastis and other cities, could no longer hold a buffer for the Levant; Aram grew from a frontier district into the power of the northern Levant, with northern Israel caught between it and Egypt. The second is the governance problem of the Omrid dynasty. Ahab's grandfather Omri had bought peace with tribute, marriage and land, absorbing Mount Carmel, Shechem and other border communities into the core of the kingdom, and Ahab's marriage to Jezebel of Sidon-Tyre brought Tyrian ships, ivory and chariot craftsmen to Samaria. That prosperity attracted two kinds of criticism at once: the prophets condemned the Baalist cult at court, while Assyrian and Aramean envoys measured how thoroughly the kingdom could be picked over. The third is the trigger. Ben-Hadad first demanded tribute with a coalition, then called for the return of cities that had been taken, and Ahab prepared to buy his way out with treasure, only to be humiliated in public at the city gate, the wealth of Samaria being compared to a handful of dust, which ended the room for negotiation. As the Aramean pressure mounted, the house of Ahab produced blood inside its own walls: the affair of Naboth's vineyard at Jezreel, in which Ahab had the owner killed in order to take the plot, put the fertile irrigated plain of Jezreel on the table at the very moment the Aramean army was on the road, and water, arable land and roads were the real prize of an Aramean advance south. The religious layer is the open clash between prophet and court. Elijah announced a drought on Mount Carmel and demanded that the Baal prophets be handed over, which declared that Ben-Hadad's network of allies and the authority of Yahweh had both failed in the face of the drought. The pride of the two kings pushed as well: the way Ben-Hadad humiliated the offered ransom turned a crisis that could have been negotiated into one that could only be settled by force.
impact: 這場戰爭留下的並非一條新界線，而是一種權力格局的位移。亞哈在阿貝克取勝、追到大馬士革城下、逼出和約，使暗利王朝的聲望遠超南方猶大的諸王：一度連大馬士革都要派人來求和，後世王朝編年把這場戰爭讀成君王涵容的模範，先知文學卻把它記成對待敗敵的失當，說明同一份戰史在不同傳統裡被引向相反的教訓。和約並沒有結束戰爭，只是結束了第一回合。哈及崛起、第二次圍城撒馬利亞、攻取迦特、削弱非利士這道屏障、耶斯列政變推倒暗利家族，一連串變化接踵而來，北以色列只能靠西頓的船與越來越多的亞述援助撐住。文本傳統把這場戰爭保存為王權模板：與敵立約、不趕盡殺絕、君王先後在軍中與朝堂，都在《申命記史家》的框架裡成為衡量暗利王朝的尺子，後來又被用來重新檢討掃羅饒過亞甲王的段落。物質層面的遺產同樣具體：撒馬利亞的車兵大隊、城內供水系統與冶鐵經濟，為王國又供應了上百年的物質底子；而亞蘭在此役所用的聯盟作戰——附庸諸王、車乘配額、一季一役的作戰節奏——在百年後成為亞述西征的標準模板。長遠看來，贏家是北方的亞述：兩代之內，昔年替埃及屏障黎凡特的強權，自己動手拆毀亞蘭與以色列的緩衝地，而這兩個為耶斯列與約旦河谷爭鬥的國家，最終淪為尼尼微的納貢行省。
impactEn: What this war left behind was not a new frontier but a shift in the balance of power. Ahab's victory at Aphek, his pursuit to the walls of Damascus and the covenant he forced out of the city gave the Omrid house a prestige that no southern king of Judah enjoyed: for a moment Damascus itself had to sue for peace. Later dynastic historiography read the campaign as a model of royal prudence, while the prophetic literature remembered the sparing of a beaten enemy as a political misjudgement, which shows the same battle history being pulled towards opposite lessons in different traditions. The treaty did not end the war, only its first round. Hazael's rise, the second siege of Samaria, the capture of Gath that broke the Philistine screen and the coup at Jezreel that felled the Omrid house all followed in turn, and the northern kingdom survived only by leaning on Tyre's ships and, increasingly, on Assyrian help. The text tradition preserved the war as a template of legitimate kingship: the covenant made with a foreign king, the refusal to finish off a defeated enemy, the king who led in the field before he governed in the palace. In the Deuteronomistic account of the Omrid dynasty these became the measures by which the house was judged, and the same narrative was later used to re-open the question of Saul sparing Agag. The material legacy was just as concrete: the chariot corps of Samaria, its water system and its iron-working economy supplied the kingdom for another century, and the coalition model Aram used in this war — client kings, quotas of chariots, one campaign season at a time — became the standard template of Assyria's own western campaigns a century later. In the long run the beneficiary was Assyria in the north. Within two generations the power that had once kept Egypt at a distance was itself dismantling the Aramean and Israelite buffer, and the two states that had fought over Jezreel and the Jordan valley were reduced to tribute-paying provinces of Nineveh.
result: 兩場戰役的結果並不一樣。第一次，以色列在阿貝克取勝，亞軍崩潰，亞捫·哈達換馬逃回大馬士革；亞哈追到亞蘭境內，兵臨城下卻攻不下，最後在城下立約、留其性命、歸還部分城邑。以色列以一次會戰的勝利換來約十年的相安，亞捫·哈達則以失去全部車馬與盟邦供應的代價換取政權存續——從此亞蘭與以色列之間形成一種「打過、也訂過約」的關係。第二次，亞捫·哈達重整旗鼓再圍撒馬利亞，饑荒與封鎖把城逼到極限，最後卻因亞軍夜間驚散而解圍；《列王紀下》把功勞歸給以利沙的預言，現代讀法則傾向認為是情報、伏擊與心理戰的合計結果。乃縵得醫治、哈及弒君登上亞蘭王位，標誌著戰局真正的轉折：接下來哈及年年在以色列境內用兵，攻破迦特、削弱非利士這道屏障，把北以色列逼到只剩耶斯列與約旦河東的退路。約蘭王在耶斯列遇刺，暗利王朝覆亡，北方王國的權力中心北移回撒馬利亞，並更依賴推羅與亞述的援助。於是這場戰爭留下的並非清晰的新界線，而是一段不穩定的均衡：以色列守住國土卻元氣大傷，亞蘭贏得霸權卻樹敵於西鄰，最終坐視北方亞述在八世紀時勢如破竹——前733年提格拉特帕拉薩爾三世再下來時，亞蘭與以色列已先後淪為亞述的屬邦。
resultEn: The two campaigns ended differently. In the first, Israel won at Aphek, the Aramean line broke, Ben-Hadad escaped on horseback to Damascus, and Ahab pursued into Aram and stood under the walls of the city without being able to take it; what finally settled the matter was a covenant made in the field, with his life spared and some of the cities returned. Israel had bought about a decade of quiet with one battle, while Ben-Hadad had bought the survival of his throne with the loss of his chariots and of the logistic support of his allies, and from then on the two states stood in a peculiar relation of war and treaty. The second time, Ben-Hadad rebuilt his army and invested Samaria again; famine and blockade brought the city to the limit, and the siege was lifted when the Aramean camp emptied itself in a night panic, which Kings attributes to the word of the prophet, while a modern reading is inclined to add up intelligence, ambush and psychological warfare. Naaman's healing and Hazael's seizure of the throne mark the real turning point. Hazael then campaigned inside Israel year after year, took Gath, weakened the Philistine screen and drove the northern kingdom back onto Jezreel and the east of the Jordan. Jehoram was killed at Jezreel, the Omrid house fell, the centre of power in the north retreated to Samaria and became more and more dependent on Tyre and on Assyrian money. The war therefore left no clean new border but an unstable equilibrium: Israel kept its territory and was exhausted, Aram held the hegemony and quarrelled with its western neighbour, and both ended by watching the northern Assyrians grow stronger, for when Tiglath-Pileser III came south again in 733 BC, Aram and Israel were already tributaries of Assyria.
